Design Rationale: The USP 645 method is met using a stand-alone analysis
(USP 645 CONDUCTIVITY) that references the user added CONDUCTIVITY 1 and CONDUCTIVITY 2 tables
to determine if the results entered for conductivity and pH are in range against a given temperature. Stage 1
components are not optional and displayed to user at the start. All subsequent stage components are optional..
and not displayed until the calculation subroutine has determined whether stage 1 has passed or failed. Stage 1.
analysis evaluation is done by the CALC CONDUCTVITY STAGE 1 subroutine, which cross references values
entered for conductivity and temperature against those in the CONDUCTIVITY 1 table. If stage 2 testing is.
needed, the user is prompted as to whether it is OK to add the additional tests. If the user answers Yes, those
analysis components are made mandatory and displayed to user for entry. Stage 2 evaluation is done by the.
CALC CONDUCTIVTY STAGE 2 subroutine, which cross references the values entered for conductivity and pH
against those in the CONDUCTIVITY_2 table. Stage 3 is the final stage, and if needed for testing, those
components are also presented to the user for entry if the user answers Yes at a second prompt warning of stage.
failure. Stage 3 and the overall conductivity readings are calculated by CALC_CONDUCTIVITY_STAGE_3 and
CALC CONDUCTIVTY FINAL respectively. The overall conductivity calculation is calculated based on all stages
entered.

Design Rationale: The USP 905 method is met using two analyses with variations, a given
product/product compound and a subroutine. The product USP_905_CU has been configured to be used as a
save as template for creating new products for this method in the future. The product table has been configured to
have PRODUCT COMPOUNDS as a child table. This child table is where key content uniformity values such as,
abel claim, dosage type, target dose, L1,L2, and lower/upper assay limits are set. Moreover, the field Content
Uniformity dosage determines the type of content uniformity (Coated tablets, transdermals, suppositories,etc) and
needs to be set accordingly for the product. This product is configured to add both the USP 905 CU DATA 1
and USP_905_CU_SUMM_1 analyses as specification tests to a sample. Both analyses are assigned with a
specific variation that matches the number of active product. Up to 5 actives are supported (5 variations). The
USP 905 CU DATA 1 analysis is added in 10 replicates for stage 1. This analysis is the data entry analysis
where users input the values for each active's content uniformity. The USP 905 CU SUMM 1 analysis is the
analysis that performs the calculations for each stage. This analysis is added in one replicate for stage 1 and all
ts components are set to calculate when the summary component calculation is triggered. The summary.
components call the CALC_CU_USP905 subroutine, which determines whether stage 1 is passed or failed

title: Calculation Block 13
content:
outright or whether stage 2 testing is needed. If stage 2 testing is needed, 20 more replicates of
USP_905_CU_DATA_1 are added to the sample for data entry and stage 2 components are switched from
optional and not displayed to mandatory and displayed on the USP 905 CU SUMM 1 analysis. Stage 2 is the
final stage and can be passed or failed. Overall content uniformity is calculated based on all stages entered.

Design Rationale: The USP 711 method is met through the use of two analyses with variations, a.
given product/product compound and a subroutine. The product USP_711_DISsO has been configured to be
used as a save as template for creating new products for this method in the future. The product table has been
configured to have PRODUCT COMPOUNDS as a child table. This child table is where key dissolution values
such as, timepoint and Q are set. This product is configured to add both the USP 711 DISS DATA 1 and
USP 711 DlSs SUMM 1 analyses as specification tests to a sample. Both analyses are assigned with a.
specific variation that matches the number of active product. Up to 5 actives are supported (5 variations). The
USP 711 DlSS DATA 1 analysis is added in 6 replicates for stage 1. This analysis is the data entry analysis
where users input the values for each active's dissolution value. The USP 711 DiSS SUMM 1 analysis is the
analysis that performs the calculation for each stage. This analysis is added in one replicate for stage 1 and all its

Desiqn Rationale: To meet FR3304, Object Group Manaqer was utilized to build a query for
worklists that are ready for review based on worklist template and then returned them in Object Group Manager.
so that a user can drill down on each worklist and perform a review utilizing the "Authorize and Close Entire.
Worklist" functionality.
Object Group Manager object "COMPLETED WORKLISTS" is created with a description of "Worklists that are
ready for approval" using Object Group Template: COMPLETED WORKLISTS. This Template utilizes a new
Data Explorer query: COMPLETED WORKLISTS and will group worklists found by Worklist Template.
When the Object Group is opened, Data Explorer is opened to prompt the user to select a worklist template by
calling new Query Tag: COMP_WORKLISTS. This query tag is configured to call new Subroutine:.
QT COMPLETED WORKLISTS. The user is first prompted to select a worklist template from a list of templates.
that are active and associated to the user's security group. If the user cancels this dialog or clicks OK without.
selecting a template, no worklists are returned in the data explorer query and subsequently within Object Group
Manager.

criteria, the user receives a message that no records were found, and nothing is returned. If worklists are found,.
then they are returned to the COMPLETD_WORKLIST Object Group Manager and grouped by Worklist.

title: Calculation Block 3
content:
This document is being issued for the gLIMs Project. The base LabWare LIMS has been tailored to support
PGS master data management requirements. This includes import/export tools to facilitate the global.
Master Data/Method Harmonization initiatives for all gLIMs Production environments as well as objects
configured for harmonization of site specific master data needs (such as subroutines)..

title: Calculation Block 6
content:
A LIMS Basic Scheduler (MASTER_DATA_IMPORT) has been configured on the EXP_RPT_MD Scheduler to run
every 30 minutes. The scheduler confirms that a background servers is defined. If a background server is
defined, background subroutine FN IMPORT MASTER DATA OBJECT is called. If no background server is
defined then subroutine FN IMPORT MASTER DATA OBJECT is called. This will ensure that if a background
server is defined, the background will always execute the work when a user manually executes the scheduler
When the subroutine is called, the subroutine will first determine the path tor where the import files need tc
be imported from. LIMS Constant (MASTER_DATA_IMPORT_DIR) contains the value of the network directory.
The current day and month are obtained as well as yesterday's day and month. The month is then formatted.
to match the folder structure, for example: January (1) would be formatted to O1-Jan. Once the file path
directory is defined, the subroutine will then obtain the number of files that are waiting to be imported for
today's date. For each of the object files found, the object and associated files for the object will be imported.
If the import functionality is unsuccessful, an error is written to the error log under a new Error Category of
MD. If the import is successful, the subroutine will determine if the object record contains the Active field. If
the record has an active field, the subroutine will confirm that the field is set to T. If the record was exported

with the Active flag as false, the flag will automatically updated to T (True) when the record is imported and an.
audit reason (Automated update from user export) is recorded for this action. Upon completion of the impori

and any associated files for the object) from the directory. If the deletion was unsuccessful, an error is recordec.
to the error log otherwise the routine loops through the process a second time for yesterday's date and if nc.
errors are found during that import loop, the process ends..

title: Calculation Block 39
content:
Database
Functions
Database functions are used to query the database. These commands are useful to get information that is not in context
For information that is in context, use the SELECT or FULL SELECT statements.
SQLSelect
The query string should be in the form:
SELECT fieldname1, fieldname2, ... FROM tablename WHERE fieldname = value.
The query string is a string variable and is defined by using double quotation marks ".
e.g.
qry1 ="SELECT name FROM analysis WHERE group_name ='DEFAULT"
Variables can be included in the query string the same way as they are included in a string variable. A string variable must have a
single quotation mark on either side of the variable (no spaces) in the query string..
e.g.
qry2 = "SELECT owner FROM project WHERE name = " + myProject + "
Numeric variables do not require single quotation marks and can use the Str function to convert the number to a string.
e.g.
qry3 = "SELECT status FROM sample WHERE sample_number = "+ Str(sampleNumber)
Query strings should be broken into different lines in order for readability..
qry4 ="SELECT status FROM sample"
e.g.

Error Trapping and Handling (cont.)
Error handling must include rollbacks to any data already changed as part of the routine.
Example:
(Concatenates the Booleans. If any false is present, false will be returned)
statusA = UpdateResultFId(sampleNumber, testNumber, resultNumber, field, value, commitFlag))
statusB = UpdateResultFId(sampleNumber, testNumber, resultNumber, field, value, commitFlag))
statusC = UpdateResultFId(sampleNumber, testNumber, resultNumber, field, value, commitFlag))
statusCheck = statusA & statusB & statusC
IF (Not(statusCheck)) THEN
RETURN "
ENDIF
It is not practical or desirable to trap every possible error since the error management code itself can introduce
errors. Assess the risk and importance of the configuration being performed and ensure appropriate measures
are in place.
LIMS basic functions that are highly likely not to fail that do not create or modify data do need not have their
return status checked.
